lead: Instruments a person owns to look at the sky, nature and the very small, and to measure weather and the world at home: telescopes and their mounts and accessories, binoculars and night optics, microscopes and magnifiers, weather and Earth instruments, sky models and historic instruments, and a home and hobby lab; organised by what you observe, with icons as archetypes at the enthusiast end and restraint at the utility end.

depts.note: Organised by optical design; Dobsonian, apochromatic refractor and SCT are archetypes within the designs, not separate kinds.

b.v: mm or inches of objective or mirror diameter
b.w: Aperture sets light grasp and resolution; every astronomy buying guide ranks it first.

b.v: achromat < ED doublet < apochromatic triplet/quadruplet (FPL-53, fluorite); mirror figure and Strehl ratio
b.w: Colour correction and figure separate premium makers (Takahashi, Tele Vue, Astro-Physics) from mass market.

b.v: fast f/2–f/5 for imaging and wide fields; slow f/8–f/15 for planets
b.w: Design choice follows target: deep sky imaging vs visual planetary.

b.v: 1.25 in / 2 in eyepiece barrels; Vixen or Losmandy dovetail; T-thread M42 and M48 back focus
b.w: Standard interfaces decide which mounts, eyepieces and cameras fit.

b.v: tube weight; grab-and-go vs observatory
b.w: The telescope used most is the one carried out most; community advice.

s.brief: Archetypes by significance. Refractor: Takahashi FSQ and FC/FOA series, Tele Vue NP101/Genesis line, Astro-Physics Starfire, William Optics RedCat and Zenithstar, Sky-Watcher Evostar/Esprit, classic achromats (Unitron, Vixen); versions are generations. Newtonian: the Dobsonian (John Dobson, Coulter Odyssey, Orion SkyQuest XT, Sky-Watcher Flextube collapsible, Obsession truss Dob), tabletop Dob (Heritage/Library Telescope), equatorial Newtonian and imaging Newtonian astrograph (types). Cassegrain: classical and Ritchey–Chrétien (GSO/Astro-Tech RC, Takahashi Mewlon Dall–Kirkham). Detail axes: aperture, focal ratio, glass, tube material. Trim mass-market starter SKUs to a handful of reference models.

k.brief: Dobsonian is the lead archetype; tabletop and truss Dobs are its versions.

s.brief: SCT: Celestron C8 (orange tube 1970 originator), C11/C14, EdgeHD, NexStar SE and CPC, Meade LX200/LX90 and ACF. Maksutov: Questar 3.5 (icon), Celestron C90, Sky-Watcher Skymax, Intes/Intes-Micro. Schmidt astrograph: Celestron RASA, historic Schmidt camera. Smart telescope: Unistellar eVscope/Odyssey, Vaonis Stellina/Vespera, ZWO Seestar, Dwarflab DWARF, Celestron Origin. Detail: aperture, optical tube vs computerised fork package, GoTo system.

Dedicated hydrogen-alpha solar telescopes: Coronado PST (icon) and SolarMax, Lunt LS series, DayStar Quark (eyepiece filter, type). White-light solar filters: Baader AstroSolar film, Thousand Oaks glass. Eclipse glasses: kind with no models, note ISO 12312-2 standard as the quality criterion. Herschel wedge and Ca-K as types of solar filter.

depts.note: Owners swap and upgrade these parts, so they keep kind-level detail; mainstream accessories are tier, premium eyepieces and mounts are variety.

b.v: kg rated vs kg carried (keep imaging load near half the rating)
b.w: Standard astrophotography advice; overloaded mounts track poorly.

b.v: periodic error in arcseconds; strain-wave vs worm gear
b.w: Decides whether long-exposure imaging works.

b.v: apparent field 50°–110°; eye relief mm
b.w: The terms eyepiece makers and reviewers compare (Tele Vue, Explore Scientific, Baader).

b.v: sensor size, pixel size, cooled or uncooled, mono or colour
b.w: Matches camera to focal length and target.

s.brief: Mount archetypes by significance: German equatorial (Losmandy G11, Sky-Watcher EQ6-R/HEQ5, Celestron CGEM/CGX, iOptron CEM, Astro-Physics Mach2/1100, 10Micron, Software Bisque Paramount), strain-wave/harmonic (ZWO AM5, iOptron HEM, Rainbow Astro), alt-az (Sky-Watcher AZ-GTi, Vixen Porta), Dobsonian base, fork. Star tracker as new kind (Sky-Watcher Star Adventurer, iOptron SkyGuider, Move Shoot Move). Merge counterweight and tube rings into one 'Mount hardware' kind with types counterweight, tube rings, dovetail bar (Vixen/Losmandy), pier extension. Tripod, wedge and polar scope: trim to reference makers (Berlebach, Milburn, QHY PoleMaster, iPolar).

k.brief: Portable camera tracking mount; new kind.
Types: optical polar scope, electronic polar camera.

s.brief: Eyepiece archetypes in order: Plössl, orthoscopic (Abbe, Baader Classic Ortho), Tele Vue Nagler (1982 originator of ultra-wide) with types/generations, Panoptic, Delos, Ethos, Explore Scientific 82°/100°, Pentax XW, Baader Morpheus/Hyperion, zoom eyepieces (Baader Hyperion Zoom, Leica ASPH zoom). Barlow and Tele Vue Powermate. Finder: Telrad, red-dot, RACI finderscope. Focuser: Crayford, rack-and-pinion, Feather Touch (Starlight Instruments), Moonlite. New kinds: star diagonal (mirror/prism, dielectric), binoviewer (Baader Maxbright, Denkmeier), collimator (Cheshire, laser, autocollimator). Dew shield gets types heater strip and dew controller.

Astronomy camera archetypes: dedicated cooled CMOS (ZWO ASI Pro, QHYCCD, Player One), planetary cameras, guide cameras (type), classic CCD (SBIG ST series) as historic versions. Filters: light-pollution/broadband (IDAS, Optolong L-Pro), narrowband (Astrodon, Chroma, Baader, Antlia), dual-band (Optolong L-eXtreme). New kinds: filter wheel (ZWO EFW, Starlight Xpress), astrophotography controller (ZWO ASIAIR, StellarMate, PrimaLuceLab Eagle). Camera adapter: T-ring, off-axis guider and field flattener as types. Focus motor: ZWO EAF, PegasusAstro FocusCube, Primaluce Sesto Senso. Cloud sensor and sky-quality meter (Unihedron SQM, Lunatico AAG CloudWatcher) stay here as observatory gear.

depts.note: Tier for everyday binoculars; variety at the alpha end where birders and hunters compare named lines.

b.v: 8x32, 8x42, 10x42, 7x50, 15x70; exit pupil = aperture ÷ magnification
b.w: The spec every binocular is named by; 8x42 is the standard birding recommendation.

b.v: budget < mid (Nikon Monarch, Vortex Viper) < alpha (Swarovski EL/NL Pure, Zeiss Victory SF, Leica Noctivid/Ultravid)
b.w: Birding and hunting reviews (Cornell Lab, Allaboutbirds, BirdWatching) group by price tier.

b.v: ED/HD/fluorite glass; phase-corrected, dielectric prism coatings; Porro vs roof
b.w: Main causes of sharpness, colour fringing and brightness differences.

b.m: Field of view and eye relief
b.v: m at 1000 m or degrees; eye relief mm for spectacle wearers
b.w: Comfort and ease of finding birds.

b.v: waterproof, nitrogen or argon purged; weight g
b.w: Outdoor use.

s.brief: Archetypes by significance: Swarovski EL (1999, versions EL Swarovision, NL Pure), Zeiss Victory SF and Zeiss 7x50 B/GA (marine classic), Leica Ultravid and Noctivid, Leica/Leitz Trinovid (historic), Nikon Monarch and Nikon EDG, Nikon 8x30 E II (Porro), Canon image-stabilised IS line, Fujinon FMT-SX (7x50 marine), Steiner military/marine, Vortex Viper/Razor, Swarovski Habicht. Types: Porro, roof, image-stabilised, compact, marine with compass. Giant binoculars: Celestron SkyMaster, Oberwerk, Fujinon 25x150, Kowa Highlander. Monocular: Zeiss Mono, Leica Monovid, Opticron. Opera glasses: types lorgnette, Galilean; antique French opera glasses (Lemaire, Chevalier) as historic archetype. Trim the 35 old models to reference lines.

Spotting scope archetypes: Swarovski ATX/STX modular and ATS, Kowa Prominar TSN-88x, Zeiss Harpia and Conquest Gavia, Leica APO-Televid, Vortex Razor HD; types angled/straight, digiscoping adapter. Night vision: PVS-14 (military monocular icon), generations Gen 1–3 and digital (types), ATN, Pulsar. Thermal: Pulsar Helion/Axion, InfiRay, HIKMICRO, FLIR Scout. Keep civilian handheld viewers; weapon sights belong to E4.

depts.note: Home, hobby and amateur microscopy; research electron and probe microscopes are out of scope.

b.v: achromat < semi-plan < plan achromat < plan apochromat; infinity vs 160 mm tube length; RMS thread
b.w: The ladder used by microscope makers and amateur microscopy forums (Micscape, Quekett).

b.v: LED Köhler illumination, Abbe condenser; darkfield, phase, polarising options
b.w: Contrast methods decide what you can see in living specimens.

b.v: stereo 7–45x; compound 40–1000x (useful max about 1000x NA)
b.w: Useful magnification is limited by numerical aperture.

b.v: aplanatic/achromatic, dioptre and magnification
b.w: Separates jewellers' and low-vision loupes from toys.

s.brief: Compound archetypes: Leitz/Zeiss Standard and Olympus CH/CH2 and BH-2 (classic used microscopes amateurs seek), Nikon Labophot/Eclipse E200, Swift, AmScope, Bresser, Euromex; Victorian brass microscopes (Powell & Lealand, Ross, Watson) as historic archetypes. Stereo: Zeiss Stemi, Leica S9, Nikon SMZ, AmScope. Digital: Dino-Lite (originator of handheld USB digital microscope), Andonstar. Pocket: Carson MicroBrite, Leuchtturm/Lensen, foldable Foldscope. Polarising (mineral hobby): Olympus BHSP/CX POL, Nikon E200POL. Merge objective, eyepiece and stage into one 'Microscope optics & parts' kind with types objective, eyepiece, condenser, stage. Slides: types plain, cavity, prepared slide sets (Victorian slide collecting as archetype if sourced). Camera: Bresser MikroCam, AmScope, Toupcam, eyepiece cameras as type.

Restraint only: tier models to market-covering makers (Eschenbach, Schweizer, Carson, Belomo, Zeiss, Bausch & Lomb). Merge folding loupe and eye loupe into one 'Loupe' kind with types folding/triplet jeweller's loupe, watchmaker's eye loupe, illuminated. Low-vision aids stay here; electronic video magnifiers belong in H2.

depts.note: Home weather stations are tier; barometers and weather glasses are collected and are variety, with antique forms as a period view.

b.v: ±°C, ±%RH; radiation shield; anemometer height
b.w: WMO siting guidance and weather-network (CWOP, Weather Underground) requirements.

b.v: console only < Wi-Fi upload < open API/local data
b.w: Enthusiasts share data to online networks.

b.v: years outdoors; replaceable sensors
b.w: Davis-class stations last decades; budget stations fail sooner.

b.v: mercury, aneroid, barograph; maker and period
b.w: Antique and maritime barometer collecting axes (auction categories).

s.brief: Tier: weather station reference makers Davis Instruments (Vantage Pro2 as archetype, Vantage Vue), Ecowitt/Fine Offset (clones Ambient Weather, Froggit, Bresser), Netatmo, La Crosse, WeatherFlow Tempest; trim the 41 models. Keep pyranometer as a 'Solar radiation sensor' kind with hobby-scale makers (Apogee) only. Wind vane: types weathervane (decorative roof vane). Windsock, rain gauge (manual CoCoRaHS gauge as reference), anemometer (handheld Kestrel as reference), hygrometer, air thermometer (max-min thermometer type) trimmed to tier makers. New kinds: Geiger counter (radiation hobby: GQ, Radex, SOEKS, Safecast bGeigie) and home seismometer (Raspberry Shake) with sources.

Barometer archetypes by significance: stick (mercury) barometer, wheel/banjo barometer, Admiral FitzRoy barometer, aneroid (Lucien Vidie 1844 originator), ship's/marine barometer, Kew-pattern; makers Negretti & Zambra, Short & Mason, Barigo, Fischer, Lufft. New kinds: barograph (Richard Frères originator, Short & Mason, Negretti & Zambra), storm glass (FitzRoy), Galileo thermometer (move the Galileo thermometer model out of air thermometer). Note antique forms for the period view; tradition entry for English barometer making if sourced.

depts.note: Models of the sky and classic observing and navigation instruments, collected new and antique; period is a view across them.

b.v: named workshop (e.g. Islamic astrolabists, Gilkerson, Trippensee, Cassens & Plath) and date
b.w: Auction and museum catalogues (Science Museum, Adler Planetarium) organise by maker and period.

b.v: original, period copy, modern reproduction, decorative replica
b.w: Many brass instruments sold today are decorative reproductions.

b.v: geared vs static; working instrument vs display
b.w: Separates working orreries and sextants from ornaments.

s.brief: Orrery (Rowley/Graham originators, Trippensee planetarium, modern geared orreries), astrolabe (planispheric astrolabe; Islamic and European traditions — add tradition entries), armillary sphere (new), celestial globe (new; makers Blaeu, Cary, Replogle), planisphere (new; Philip's, David Chandler, Miller), home planetarium projector (Sega Toys Homestar with Takayuki Ohira as originator of the home line, Megastar professional excluded), sextant (new; types octant; Cassens & Plath, Heath, Davis Mark 15 plastic, Tamaya). Only include archetypes with sources.

depts.note: Only what amateurs, home brewers, mycologists and students own; industrial and research lab equipment is out of scope.

b.v: soda-lime < borosilicate 3.3 (Duran, Pyrex, Kimax)
b.w: Borosilicate survives heating; standard lab supply guidance.

b.v: Class B < Class A volumetric ware; balance readability 0.1 g to 0.001 g
b.w: ISO/ASTM classes printed on the ware.

s.brief: Restraint: trim to market-covering makers (DWK Duran/Kimax, Corning Pyrex, Brand, Hirschmann, Eppendorf, Gilson). Merge conical and volumetric flasks into 'Laboratory flask' (types Erlenmeyer, volumetric, Florence). Merge round-bottom flask and condenser into 'Distillation glassware' (types round-bottom flask, Liebig/Allihn/Graham condenser, still head). Merge burette into pipette as type. Prefer hobby-scale models over research SKUs.

Restraint: keep hobby-scale models only (milligram/jewellery-scale balances, magnetic stirrers used for yeast starters, mini centrifuges, small incubators, laminar-flow hoods used by mushroom growers); drop research-grade SKUs (Beckman Allegra/Avanti, BINDER, Memmert lines) and keep the kind with few or no models.

drop.why: Electron microscopes are institutional; owner finding says out.
Scanning probe microscopes are research instruments.
Laboratory oven: institutional; home use covered by kitchen ovens.
Laboratory autoclave: institutional; hobbyists use pressure cookers (B5).
Inert-atmosphere glove box: research lab only.
